did_you_know.text: Did you know? The name "Korach" is derived from a root meaning baldness or ice, and some interpret this as a hint to his arrogance and 'rising above' the community.

Did you know? Of all the rebellion leaders mentioned in this verse, "On son of Pelet" is the only one not mentioned again. Rabbinic sages explain that his wife saved him by convincing him to withdraw from the rebellion.

Did you know? The 250 "princes of the congregation, called to the assembly" were not common people, but heads of ancestral houses and prominent leaders chosen for important councils, showing the rebellion's strength.

Did you know? The phrase "Rav Lakhem" (רב לכם) means "enough for you" or "you've gone too far," reflecting the rebels' claim that Moses and Aaron were exceeding their authority or taking too much honor for themselves.
Did you know? Offering incense was an act exclusively permitted to priests from Aaron's lineage. Moses' challenge to the rebels to offer incense was a direct test of their claim to the priesthood.

Did you know? Korach and the Kehatites were Levites whose duty was to carry the holy vessels of the Tabernacle. Moses reminded them that this role itself was a great honor, bringing them close to God's service.
Did you know? Dathan and Abiram use the phrase "land flowing with milk and honey" sarcastically to accuse Moses of leading them from Egypt, which they claimed was good, into the barren desert.

Did you know? In Moses' statement, "I have not taken one donkey from them," he emphasizes that he never abused his authority to seize property from the people, unlike some other ancient Near Eastern leaders.

Did you know? The appeal "God, God of the spirits of all flesh" highlights Moses and Aaron's recognition of God as the source of all life and souls, and it's a plea for Him not to punish everyone for the sin of a few.

Did you know? The command for the congregation to move away from the dwellings of Korach, Dathan, and Abiram illustrates the principle of collective responsibility, but also the ability of individuals to separate themselves to be saved.

Did you know? Moses describes an unprecedented and supernatural punishment that would be a "new creation" – the earth swallowing living people – to prove that the rebellion was against God Himself, not just him.

Did you know? The punishments in Korach's rebellion were twofold: the earth swallowed Korach, Dathan, Abiram, their families, and possessions, while fire from the Lord consumed the 250 incense offerers.
